findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5076 is "Fix hostnames on UFs" (rectify_hostname), unrelated to Nutanix. There is no "Splunk Add-on for Nutanix Prism". The Nutanix-published add-ons are "TA for Nutanix Prism Central" (TA-nutanix-PC, 8349) and "TA for Nutanix Prism" (TA-nutanix, 3103). The wrong ID and name recur in app, dataSources, implementation, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Reference TA for Nutanix Prism Central (Splunkbase 8349, TA-nutanix-PC) for Prism Central, or TA-nutanix (3103) for Prism Element, and fix the reference link.

findings.explanation: In the Prism Central v3 alerts schema, fields sit under `status.resources`: `severity`, `title`, `creation_time`, `impact_type_list`, `resolution_status.is_true`, `acknowledged_status.is_true`, `affected_entity_list`, and `source_entity.cluster_uuid`. There is no `is_resolved`/`is_acknowledged`, no `impact_types` and no `context_attributes.cluster_name`. The sample JSON in detailedImplementation repeats the invented shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the real v3 paths, note that only cluster_uuid is returned (cluster name needs a lookup from clusters/list or the TA's cluster feed), and correct the sample event.

findings.explanation: The sourcetype names are tied to a non-existent add-on and do not match the repository guide (`nutanix:alert`). The text also describes "2.x or 3.x" TA generations without evidence.
findings.quote: sourcetype in (`nutanix:prism_central:alerts` primary) with defensive ORs to `nutanix:alerts:v3` and `nutanix:alerts` for older Splunk Add-on for Nutanix Prism (5076) builds
findings.suggested_fix: Check the TA-nutanix-PC user guide on the Nutanix portal (NTNX-prism-central-splunk-application-user-guide) for the alert sourcetype and replace the guessed names.

findings.explanation: The generic maintenance, batch and synthetic-probe scenarios do not name real Prism alert noise, such as alerts raised during one-click AOS/LCM upgrades, NCC check alerts that auto-resolve, or alerts left unresolved but stale in Prism.

findings.suggested_fix: List Nutanix-specific noise sources (LCM/AOS upgrade windows, host maintenance mode, auto-resolving NCC checks, PCVM-originated alerts without a cluster) and how to suppress each.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The SPL reads is_resolved/resolved, is_acknowledged, impact_types and cluster_name, none of which exist in the v3 alert payload (resolution_status.is_true, acknowledged_status.is_true, impact_type_list, source_entity.cluster_uuid). The resolved filter then defaults every alert to unresolved, ack is always 0, top_impact is unknown, and cluster collapses to __pcvm_self__.

The unresolved filter runs before `dedup alert_id`, and the search has no explicit time bound. A resolved alert's last earlier unresolved poll is still kept, so resolved alerts stay on the list until they age out of the window. Dedup to the latest event per alert first, then filter on resolution state.

summary: The UC names the wrong Splunkbase add-on (5076 is a hostname-fixing app, not Nutanix) and documents a Prism Central v3 alert JSON shape that does not match the published v3 schema, so the SPL field names will not resolve. Templated description, controlTest and false-positive text add little.
